name: Libya (divided: GNU Tripoli and LNA/HoR east)

areaKm2.note: asOf 2024. Surface area 1,759,540 km2 (AG.SRF.TOTL.K2); low is land area 1,759,540 km2 (AG.LND.TOTL.K2).

population.note: asOf 2025 (World Bank SP.POP.TOTL 7,458,555). Low -1% / high +1.5% for 2026 growth and estimate uncertainty.

activePersonnel.note: Military of Libya infobox: ~32,000 Libyan Armed Forces (GNU, Tripoli) + ~90,000 Libyan Arab Armed Forces (LNA, Haftar) = 122,000 combined; the two are rival forces. LNA article gives 85,000+ (2020). Low reflects militias counted loosely.

trainedReserves.note: Educated guess. No organised reserve on either side; high allows for tribal and militia call-ups.

supportPersonnel.note: Active 122,000 minus infantry P roles (90,000). Covers air arms, navies, logistics and staff of both sides.

mobilizationRatio.note: Analogy to 2011 and 2019-20 civil-war peaks (~100,000-150,000 combatants of ~6.5 million, ~2%); scaled to 1.5-5%.

gdpPerCapita.note: asOf 2025. GDP 84,293,786,108 2011 int$ (World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD rebased x 0.8005) / population 7,458,555 = 11,302 2011 int$. Range +/-15%. Oil output swings with blockades. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

gdp.note: asOf 2025. World Bank NY.GDP.MKTP.PP.KD (constant 2021 int$) 105,301,419,248 x 0.8005 (US GDP deflator 2011/2021) = 84,293,786,108 2011 int$. Range +/-15% for PPP benchmark uncertainty and the relative-price drift the rebase ignores. Oil output swings with blockades. Corrected 2026-10-29: values x1.0376 because the rebase factor was an arithmetic error (0.8005); the right factor is 0.8306 (FRED GDPDEF, 2017=100: 2011 91.478 / 2021 110.130). Figures quoted above are before the correction.

milSpendShare.note: SIPRI via World Bank: 3.57% of GDP in 2023, 2.80% 2022. Two parallel administrations; foreign-funded equipment not counted (high).

industrialShare.note: asOf 2025: industry incl. construction (and hydrocarbons) 73.2% of GDP (NV.IND.TOTL.ZS). Range +/-7% for oil-price swings. Oil and gas dominate.

foodSurplus.note: Recomputed 2026-10-29 under the definition: 0.02 -> 0.53. Formula: surplus = 1 - a/s, a = farm population share of consumers (proxy: agricultural employment share, World Bank SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS, ILO modelled, https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/LBY/indicator/SL.AGR.EMPL.ZS), s = domestic production / consumption (calorie self-sufficiency). a = 10.00% (2025). s from FAOSTAT Food Balance Sheets (https://bulks-faostat.fao.org/production/FoodBalanceSheets_E_All_Data.zip): production / domestic supply summed over all FBS items, each weighted by kcal per tonne (world median of food kcal / food tonnes per item); feed, processing and non-food uses stay in domestic supply. s = 0.21 (mean 2021-2023, range 0.19-0.23). Mid 1 - 0.100/0.21 = 0.53. Low: a x 1.3 (farm households larger than the employed count), s 0.19 = 0.3. High: s 0.23 = 0.57. Import dependence: domestic production covers about 21% of domestic calorie supply. Earlier net-trade reading: Educated guess. Imports ~75% of food.

annualCohort.note: asOf 2025. Males reaching military age per year = male population 3,791,703 x share of males aged 15-19 9.311% (SP.POP.1519.MA.5Y) / 5 = 70,613. Male population from SP.POP.TOTL.MA.IN. Males only (conscript-pool convention). Range +/-10% for single-year cohort variation.

roadKm.note: asOf 2010: 37,000 km in the road network list; World Bank IS.ROD.TOTL.KM gave 83,200 km (2000) on a broader definition (high). Mid is between them.

railKm.note: CIA Factbook lists no railways; Libyan rail projects stalled in 2011.

majorPorts.note: CIA Factbook 2024: 14 ports, 0 large, 2 medium; key ports Tripoli, Benghazi, Misrata, Tobruk, Marsa el Brega.

merchantTonnage.note: asOf 2025: not in the list of flags over 1,000,000 GT, so under ~1.6 million DWT; mid is an educated guess.

supplyRangeKm.note: Educated guess. Coastal road logistics, long desert lines to the Fezzan.

draftAnimals.note: Educated guess. Camels, donkeys; not from FAO data.

nuclearWarheads.note: Libya is not listed among the nine nuclear-armed states in the FAS Status of World Nuclear Forces 2026 table. Weapons programme abandoned in 2003.

homeDefense.note: Rubric 1.2: vast desert and urban militias; 1.3 high for the Sahara depth.

notes: DIVIDED-STATE snapshot: Libya has two rival armed forces since 2014: the UN-recognised Government of National Unity in Tripoli with its Libyan Armed Forces and allied militias (~32,000 regulars, Turkish-backed), and Khalifa Haftar's Libyan Arab Armed Forces / LNA in the east and south (~90,000, backed by Russia's Africa Corps, the UAE and Egypt), per the Military of Libya article. Forces here are the SUM of both sides (one ne:LBY polygon) and so overstate what either government can use against an outsider; cohesion and command are rated accordingly. Equipment counts are educated guesses (grade D) except the IISS 2020 tank and combat-aircraft totals. Turkish, Russian and other foreign forces are not counted. asOf 2025 economic data.
